primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Vitamin C is required for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases during intracellular collagen processing; deficiency produces unstable collagen and reduced tensile strength.
vignette: A man with a highly restricted diet develops perifollicular hemorrhages, corkscrew hairs, bleeding gums, and poor wound healing.
lead: Which intracellular step in collagen synthesis is most directly impaired?
correct: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in the rough endoplasmic reticulum
distractors: Extracellular cleavage of procollagen terminal peptides
Translation of preprocollagen on free cytosolic ribosomes
Extracellular assembly of tropocollagen into fibrils
distractor_notes: Procollagen peptide cleavage is extracellular and not vitamin C dependent.
Lysyl oxidase requires copper, not vitamin C.
Collagen is translated on RER-bound ribosomes, and vitamin C deficiency does not block translation itself.
Fibril assembly occurs extracellularly and is secondary to the defective hydroxylation.
key_expl: Ascorbate is a cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases in the RER. Deficiency impairs hydroxylation, destabilizing the collagen triple helix and causing tissue fragility.
objective: Link scurvy to impaired vitamin C-dependent proline/lysine hydroxylation during collagen synthesis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of coagulation factors
mechanism: Reduced vitamin K is a cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which converts glutamate residues to gamma-carboxyglutamate so vitamin K-dependent clotting proteins can bind calcium.
vignette: A patient with severe fat malabsorption develops easy bruising and prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency.
correct: Gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues on vitamin K-dependent proteins
distractors: Hydroxylation of proline residues in collagen
Phosphorylation of serine residues on fibrinogen
Sulfation of tyrosine residues on albumin
Acetylation of lysine residues on factor VIII
distractor_notes: Proline hydroxylation is vitamin C dependent.
This is not the vitamin K-dependent coagulation modification.
Albumin sulfation is not the relevant mechanism.
Factor VIII is not activated by vitamin K-dependent lysine acetylation.
key_expl: Vitamin K supports gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues on factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S, allowing calcium binding and membrane localization.
objective: Explain why vitamin K deficiency impairs coagulation through loss of gamma-carboxylation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury during thyroidectomy
mechanism: The recurrent laryngeal nerve courses near the thyroid in the tracheoesophageal groove and supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid.
vignette: After thyroidectomy, a patient develops new hoarseness and unilateral vocal cord paralysis.
lead: Which nerve was most likely injured?
distractors: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
distractor_notes: External superior laryngeal injury primarily impairs cricothyroid function and pitch.
Internal superior laryngeal provides supraglottic sensation.
CN IX does not innervate intrinsic laryngeal muscles.
CN XII innervates tongue muscles.
key_expl: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is vulnerable during thyroidectomy and innervates nearly all intrinsic laryngeal muscles; injury can cause vocal cord paralysis and hoarseness.
objective: Identify recurrent laryngeal nerve injury as the cause of postoperative vocal cord paralysis after thyroid surgery.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Medial scapular winging from long thoracic nerve injury
mechanism: Long thoracic nerve injury paralyzes serratus anterior, impairing scapular protraction and fixation to the thoracic wall and causing medial winging accentuated by wall pushing.
vignette: After axillary surgery, a patient has prominent medial scapular winging when pushing against a wall and difficulty elevating the arm above horizontal.
lead: Which nerve is most likely injured?
distractor_notes: Spinal accessory injury weakens trapezius and causes a different winging pattern.
Dorsal scapular injury affects rhomboids.
Suprascapular injury affects supraspinatus/infraspinatus.
Axillary injury affects deltoid and teres minor.
key_expl: The long thoracic nerve innervates serratus anterior. Loss of serratus anterior causes medial scapular winging and impaired upward rotation/protraction.
objective: Recognize long thoracic nerve injury from the classic serratus anterior palsy examination.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Meckel diverticulum from persistent vitelline duct
mechanism: Incomplete obliteration of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct leaves a true diverticulum on the antimesenteric ileum.
vignette: A young child has painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding. Imaging identifies a blind-ending pouch arising from the antimesenteric border of the distal ileum.
lead: Failure of obliteration of which embryologic structure caused this lesion?
distractor_notes: Urachal persistence produces urachal anomalies between bladder and umbilicus.
The urachus derives from the allantoic connection and does not form Meckel diverticulum.
Pancreatic buds form the pancreas.
Paramesonephric ducts form female reproductive structures.
key_expl: Meckel diverticulum results from incomplete regression of the vitelline/omphalomesenteric duct and is a true diverticulum of the antimesenteric ileum.
objective: Identify persistent vitelline duct as the embryologic basis of Meckel diverticulum.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: DiGeorge syndrome from abnormal pharyngeal apparatus and neural crest development
mechanism: 22q11.2/TBX1 haploinsufficiency disrupts pharyngeal apparatus development and cardiac neural crest migration, producing thymic/parathyroid hypoplasia and conotruncal defects.
vignette: A newborn has truncus arteriosus, hypocalcemia, and recurrent viral/fungal infections due to thymic hypoplasia.
lead: Abnormal development of which embryologic structures best explains this constellation?
correct: Third and fourth pharyngeal pouches with associated cardiac neural crest development
distractor_notes: First cleft forms external auditory canal structures.
Second arch defects do not produce the classic thymus/parathyroid/conotruncal combination.
Dorsal mesogastrium is unrelated.
Mesonephric ducts form male genital tract derivatives.
key_expl: DiGeorge/22q11.2 deletion syndrome disrupts development of third/fourth pharyngeal pouch derivatives and cardiac neural crest-associated outflow tract structures.
objective: Connect thymic hypoplasia, hypocalcemia, and conotruncal disease to 22q11.2-related pharyngeal apparatus defects.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Alport syndrome from type IV collagen alpha-chain defects
mechanism: Mutations in COL4A3/4/5 disrupt the type IV collagen alpha345 network in glomerular, cochlear, and ocular basement membranes.
vignette: A teenage boy has persistent hematuria, progressive sensorineural hearing loss, and a family history of renal failure in maternal male relatives.
lead: Which structural protein is most likely abnormal?
distractor_notes: Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta and related disorders.
Type II collagen is prominent in cartilage.
Fibrillin-1 defects cause Marfan syndrome.
Elastin defects do not explain the renal-hearing basement membrane phenotype.
key_expl: Most X-linked Alport syndrome involves COL4A5, disrupting type IV collagen in GBM, cochlea, and eye; classic manifestations include hematuria and sensorineural hearing loss.
objective: Recognize type IV collagen defects as the molecular basis of Alport syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Pemphigus vulgaris from anti-desmoglein antibodies disrupting desmosomes
mechanism: IgG antibodies against desmoglein 3 and often desmoglein 1 disrupt desmosomal keratinocyte adhesion, causing intraepidermal acantholysis.
vignette: A middle-aged patient develops painful oral erosions and flaccid skin bullae that rupture easily; Nikolsky sign is positive.
lead: Autoantibodies are directed against proteins in which cell junction?
distractor_notes: Hemidesmosomes anchor basal keratinocytes to basement membrane and are targeted in bullous pemphigoid.
Tight junctions regulate paracellular permeability.
Gap junctions mediate intercellular communication.
Focal adhesions link cells to extracellular matrix through integrins.
key_expl: Pemphigus vulgaris is caused by IgG against desmogleins, cadherins within desmosomes; loss of keratinocyte adhesion produces acantholytic, flaccid intraepidermal blisters.
objective: Link pemphigus vulgaris to autoantibody-mediated disruption of desmosomal desmogleins.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Nonshivering thermogenesis through UCP1 in brown adipose tissue
mechanism: UCP1 dissipates the mitochondrial proton gradient as heat instead of coupling proton reentry to ATP synthesis, enabling sympathetic cold-induced thermogenesis.
vignette: A healthy newborn exposed to a cool environment maintains body temperature largely through nonshivering thermogenesis.
lead: Which mitochondrial process is most directly responsible?
correct: Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation by allowing proton reentry without ATP synthesis
distractors: Inhibition of electron transport at complex IV
distractor_notes: Complex IV inhibition reduces energy production and is toxic.
Brown fat deliberately reduces coupling efficiency.
Fatty-acid oxidation supplies fuel for thermogenesis.
Sympathetic activation stimulates brown fat thermogenesis.
key_expl: Brown adipose mitochondria express UCP1, which permits protons to cross the inner mitochondrial membrane without driving ATP synthase. The stored electrochemical energy is released as heat.
objective: Explain neonatal nonshivering thermogenesis through UCP1-mediated mitochondrial uncoupling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Left gastric artery injury along the lesser curvature of the stomach
mechanism: The left gastric artery, a direct branch of the celiac trunk, runs along the superior lesser curvature and anastomoses with the right gastric artery.
vignette: During surgery on the proximal lesser curvature of the stomach, an artery arising directly from the celiac trunk is accidentally ligated.
lead: Which artery was most likely injured?
distractor_notes: Right gastroepiploic runs along the greater curvature.
Left gastroepiploic also supplies the greater curvature.
Gastroduodenal passes posterior to the first duodenum.
Short gastric arteries supply the fundus from the splenic artery.
key_expl: The left gastric artery is one of the three primary celiac branches and courses along the lesser curvature, where it anastomoses with the right gastric artery.
objective: Identify the left gastric artery from its origin and course along the stomach's lesser curvature.
